text:
Matthew Knies has been the Columbus story: 30 headlines in two weeks, most of them about his return to Toronto, a dramatic Blue Jackets win there, and a jab at his old fan base afterward. Zach Werenski scored the winner that night and set another franchise record with two points. It was the best evening of a hard month.

The standings are the bad news. Columbus is 9-13-1 with 19 points, 3-6-1 in its last 10, and our simulations give it an 8% chance at the playoffs. Some of that is the puck refusing to go in. The Blue Jackets have scored almost 11 fewer goals than their chances deserved, and they sit 3.4 points below their expected points. Charlie Coyle has two points in his last 10 games against 8.1 our numbers expected; that kind of drought rarely lasts.

But the process is not good enough to wait on. They get 48% of the expected goals at 5v5 and score 2.43 goals a game. The Werenski and Damon Severson pair has been on for 20 goals for and 10 against, yet holds only 48% of the chances. The most promising line is Knies with Kent Johnson and Luca Del Bel Belluz: 58% of the expected goals, outscoring teams 7-1.

Cam Talbot has become the workhorse in net. What to watch: whether the finishing turns before the season is gone.
headline: Knies found a home, the goals didn't follow
